# magpie-gemini-web [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/magpie-gemini-web?style=flat-square&logo=npm&color=4f46e5)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/magpie-gemini-web) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/magpie-gemini-web?style=flat-square&color=06b6d4)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/magpie-gemini-web) [![Magpie Plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Magpie-Plugin-3b82f6?style=flat-square)](https://usemagpie.ai/) [![Node.js >= 22](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-8b5cf6?style=flat-square&logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](https://nodejs.org/) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20Windows-6366f1?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-10b981?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [中文](README.md) | English Use **Google AI Studio** and **Gemini on the web** through your Google account in [Magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/). The plugin runs [AIStudio2API](https://github.com/Mag1cFall/AIStudio2API) and [gemini-web2api-go](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go) locally, turning Google web interfaces into OpenAI-compatible APIs. > **2026-10-16 update:** Full-price Google AI Pro accounts can now use `gemini-4-argon` directly in Antigravity, and can likewise be proxied directly with Magpie. ## Which Provider Should I Choose? The plugin provides two independent providers that can be used individually or together: | Feature | Google AI Studio (`ai-studio`) | Gemini Web (`gemini-web`) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Best for** | **Coding agents (recommended)** | General chat, web-only models & web quota | | **Tool calling** | **Native Function Calling**, reliable | Prompt-emulated (experimental; Flash often skips tools) | | **Thinking levels** | Supported levels from the model catalog: `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` | `low` (base) / `medium` (`-thinking-medium`, `gemini-4-argon` only) / `high` (`-thinking` extended thinking) | | **Image input** | On by default; chat models read images | On by default; chat models read images (needs a signed-in cookie) | | **Image generation** | Nano Banana models, for Magpie's image generation (Magpie v0.1.2075+, see below) | Not supported | | **Sign-in method** | Chrome / cookie / browser import with automatic configuration | Copy `cookie` from a private/incognito window | | **Usage cards** | Shows models currently on cooldown and recovery times | Syncs **5-hour** & **weekly** usage and reset times from the web | | **Local backend** | AIStudio2API (`v0.3.5`) | gemini-web2api-go (`4.28.0-magpie.1` optimized build) | --- ## Quick Start Install **magpie-gemini-web** from the Magpie plugin market, then sign in to either (or both) providers below. The plugin automatically downloads the corresponding backend, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and runs it in the background—no Go installation or extra setup required. ### Option 1: Google AI Studio (`ai-studio`) 1. Sign in to **Google AI Studio** in Magpie and choose **「用 Google 账号登录（推荐）」** (Sign in with a Google account). 2. Once the plugin prepares the local service, the same tab automatically opens **account import / sign-in**. Choose **Chrome import, paste cookies, or browser login**. No separate installation or API key copying is needed; select multiple accounts once in the import UI. 3. When every item in this sign-in task succeeds, the plugin **automatically configures Magpie**. A single import saves that account; a batch saves the imported group, retaining earlier successes when only failed accounts are retried. There is no return-and-select step, and the existing `ai-studio` provider, models, image generation and usage cards remain available. 4. **Managing accounts:** Sign in again to add an account, create a separate card for an existing account, or re-authenticate. **「直接打开 Google 登录窗口」** (Open Google login window directly) retains the isolated browser login flow. The local service (~40 MB) is downloaded on first use. Browser login and the dedicated reauthentication entry require Camoufox (~300 MB). You can also use Add Google Account to import the same account from Chrome, cookies, or a debugging browser, updating its login state while preserving file bindings and renewal credentials. Magpie waits up to 10 minutes, downloads included. In the automatic flow, timeout or cancellation stops this sign-in's unfinished tasks and preserves imported accounts; tasks from other windows are unaffected. Set `studio.proxy` first if GitHub is unreachable. Bundled backend `0.3.5-magpie.1` includes automatic sign-in. An older running backend retains the manual connection flow; after it is stopped, the next managed startup upgrades it. ### Option 2: Gemini Web (`gemini-web`) 1. Sign in to **Gemini Web** in Magpie and choose **「一键配置本地 Gemini Web（推荐）」** (One-click local setup). If you need a proxy to reach Google, enter its URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7890`) when prompted at the start of sign-in, or leave it blank for direct connection / existing proxy pool. 2. Enter the **Google account index** when prompted: for `/u/4/app` in the same window you copy cookies from, enter `4`; leave it blank for a single-account session (`0`). Private windows may assign different indices from your regular browser. Copy your cookie using a **private / incognito window** (Firefox recommended): 1. Open in the private window and sign in to your Google account. 2. Press `F12` (`⌥⌘I` on macOS), switch to the **Network** tab, and reload the page. 3. Click any `gemini.google.com` request → **Headers** → **Request Headers**, copy the `cookie` value, and paste it into Magpie. 4. **Close the private window directly—do not sign out** (signing out invalidates the cookie). 3. The plugin verifies the account and completes sign-in. Repeat the steps above to add more accounts. > **Backend upgrade required during sign-in?** An older background process may still be running. Exit Magpie, stop the matching `gemini-web2api-go` process (Windows: Task Manager → Details → `gemini-web2api-go.exe`), then run the full installation command shown in the error. It preserves accounts and configuration and selects the plugin's managed backend. Set `GEMINI_WEB_PROXY` first if the download needs a proxy. Reopen Magpie and sign in after installation. > **Why is a private window required?** The backend periodically refreshes this session to keep it alive. If it shares a session with your daily browser, Google will revoke the session and sign your browser out of all Google services. A private window (or a dedicated secondary Google account) gives the backend an isolated session. --- ## Multiple Accounts & Usage Cards - **Account usage cards:** Individual accounts use their email address. An AI Studio batch gets a separate group card; importing the same group in a different order keeps its identity. - *Migrating older Gemini Web accounts:* For accounts added in earlier versions, add a Gemini Web account in Magpie and choose **「添加本地后端里已有的 Google 账号」** (Add an existing Google account from the local backend) to create individual cards, then remove the old pooled `API key …` card. - **Automatic account rotation:** The local backend selects which Google account serves each request (Gemini Web rotates across the pool; AI Studio uses one account until cooldown and switches to the next, with optional account priority order and per-model account bindings configurable in the admin page or via `studio.accountOrder` and `studio.modelAccounts`). Switching cards in Magpie does not change which account the backend picks. - **Usage reporting:** - `gemini-web`: Available only with the one-click local backend. Usage is read from Google again whenever Magpie asks for it (at most once every 30 seconds per account), so pressing refresh shows the current allowance, including usage from the Gemini app, the website or other devices. On its own, Magpie asks about once a minute while the Usage page or the menu bar's allowances panel is open, whenever it updates allowances shown in the menu bar (every 3 minutes by default), and at most once a minute while it routes requests among accounts; otherwise it doesn't ask. A failed read isn't retried on its own for 10 minutes; pressing refresh in that time retries it at once (press it again if the first press doesn't). - `ai-studio`: AI Studio does not report remaining total quota; cards display models currently on cooldown and their recovery times, or prompt when re-authentication is needed. --- ## Image Generation (AI Studio) `ai-studio` lists the Nano Banana image models your account can use (such as `gemini-3.1-flash-image` and `gemini-3-pro-image`), for Magpie's image generation. **This needs Magpie v0.1.2075 or later**, the first to take a plugin's Gemini image models as models that draw. **Drawing from an agent** (pi, Claude Code, Codex and the rest alike): 1. **Pick the model to draw with:** Magpie's Settings list these models under **Images → Image generation**. Pick one (such as `ai-studio/gemini-nano-banana-2.1`), or leave it on Automatic. There's no need to tick them in any model list. 2. **Give the agent the drawing tool:** click **Give agents Magpie Image…** under that row, tick the agents that should draw in the Library it opens, then start a new session in the agent. With the Library turned off, the row says **Turn on the Library** instead: click that first. From the command line: `magpie library mcp add magpie-image magpie mcp image agents=pi` (several agents separated by commas, as in `agents=pi,claude`). 3. **Chat as usual:** keep the agent on its usual chat model and ask it to draw something. It calls the `generate_image` tool, which draws with the model from step 1 and saves the image in the project's `generated-images/` folder; reference images make it an edit. - **Don't pick an image model as the chat model:** Magpie still keeps a plugin's models that draw in its chat model lists ([yetone/magpie#2792](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2792)). Picked there, they show no picture: an agent such as pi has no place for an image in the model's reply, so the image the model draws is dropped, while the model believes it was shown. They take no tool calls either, and have 32K–128K context windows. - **Drawing from the command line:** `magpie tool generate_image "a magpie on a branch, watercolour" --size 16:9 -o magpie.png`; add `--model ai-studio/gemini-3-pro-image` to draw with another model this once. If the terminal can't find the `magpie` command (step 2's command too), click **Add to PATH** on the **Command line** row of Magpie's Settings, then open a new terminal. - **Size:** `size` gives the aspect ratio. A ratio (such as `16:9` or `1:4`) is used as it is when the model takes it, else the nearest one it does; a size such as `1536x1024` is made the nearest usual ratio by Magpie first. `quality` makes no difference for these models. - If you don't want the image models, turn them off with `studio.imageModels` (see the options below). --- ## Configuration & Advanced Usage
⚙️ Plugin Options & Proxy Setup (image input, proxy configuration, custom backends)
Tool calling and image input are enabled by default. Configure plugin options via the CLI: ```bash # Turn image input off only for Gemini Web, keeping it on for AI Studio magpie plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{"allowImages":false,"studio":{"allowImages":true}}' # Turn image input off for AI Studio magpie plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{"studio":{"allowImages":false}}' # Configure a proxy for AI Studio magpie plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{"studio":{"proxy":"http://127.0.0.1:7890"}}' ``` > **Windows PowerShell**: `magpie` runs the `magpie.cmd` wrapper, which loses the double quotes inside the JSON when it passes the arguments on. Call the program behind it directly instead: it is in the same folder as `magpie.cmd` (which `where.exe magpie` finds), named something like `magpie-windows-amd64.exe`, and Magpie's Settings > Command line shows it too. How to write it depends on the PowerShell version (`$PSVersionTable.PSVersion` shows it): > - PowerShell 7.3 or later, default settings: `& "" plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{"allowImages":true}'` > - Windows PowerShell 5.1 (built into Windows): it doesn't escape the double quotes in an argument for you, so write them as `\"`: `& "" plugin options magpie-gemini-web '{\"allowImages\":true}'` | Option | Default | Scope | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `allowTools` | `true` | Shared (override via `studio.allowTools`) | Allow tool calls. When `false`, requests with tools return 400 | | `allowImages` | `true` | Shared (override via `studio.allowImages`) | Allow image input in a chat (an image model's reference images don't need it). Gemini Web reads images only when signed in and returns 400 otherwise | | `requestTimeoutMs` / `modelTimeoutMs` | Web: `570000` / `10000`; Studio: `1800000` / `10000` | Shared (override via `studio.*`) | Timeout (ms) per backend wait or model list fetch; resets on stream data, explicit settings take precedence | | `stripCitations` | `true` | `gemini-web` only | Strip `[cite: 1]` and `[cite_start]` markers from replies and tool arguments (not supported on AI Studio) | | `proxy` | none | `gemini-web` only | Proxy for the managed Gemini Web backend to reach Google (`http` / `https` / `socks5` / `socks5h`), or set `GEMINI_WEB_PROXY` env var / enter during sign-in | | `baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1` | `gemini-web` only | Default Gemini Web backend URL | | `contextLimit` / `outputLimit` | `1000000` / `8192` | `gemini-web` only | Context and output limits reported to clients | | `studio.proxy` | none | `ai-studio` only | Proxy for reaching Google (`http` / `https` / `socks5`), or set `AI_STUDIO_PROXY` env var; when set, it takes precedence over the proxy saved in the admin page. An empty value counts as unset | | `studio.accountOrder` | none | `ai-studio` only | Account priority order (comma-separated string or string array, e.g. `["b@gmail.com","a@gmail.com"]`); seeds `ACCOUNT_ORDER` in `.env` when unset, while preserving any non-empty value saved in the admin page | | `studio.modelAccounts` | none | `ai-studio` only | Per-model account bindings (`"model:acc1|acc2"` string or `{ "gemini-3.1-pro-preview": ["acc1", "acc2"] }` object); seeds `MODEL_ACCOUNTS` in `.env` when unset, while preserving any non-empty value saved in the admin page | | `studio.baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:2048/v1` | `ai-studio` only | Default URL when connecting an existing AIStudio2API instance | | `studio.contextLimit` / `studio.outputLimit` | Model catalog defaults | `ai-studio` only | Limits reported to clients (can only lower the catalog defaults) | | `studio.imageModels` | `true` | `ai-studio` only | List the Nano Banana image models, for Magpie's image generation; `false` lists text models only | **Using a proxy to reach Google:** - **AI Studio:** Preferably set it in the local admin page. Open the address on the usage card's "管理页" (admin page) line (default `http://127.0.0.1:2048`) and sign in as `magpie` with `adminPassword` from `config.json` in the data directory. Save the proxy, then restart the service from the admin page. The plugin keeps the saved value when it restarts the backend. - Alternatively, `studio.proxy` or `AI_STUDIO_PROXY` take precedence over the saved proxy. A change applies after the local service restarts (`npm run studio:stop`; the next request starts it again). - With none set, the backend goes out directly, or through the system proxy on macOS and Windows. - **The backend uses neither Magpie's proxies (including the provider proxy set for `ai-studio`) nor `HTTPS_PROXY` and similar variables**: it keeps running after Magpie quits, when a proxy borrowed from Magpie may be gone. Use one of the options above. A backend started by a plugin version from before this fix may still be using a proxy from the environment it was started in (Magpie's, for example); the "代理出口" line marks it and says what a restart changes. - The usage card's "代理出口" (proxy) line, the Google sign-in instructions and failure messages, and `npm run studio:status` show the proxy the backend actually uses, where it comes from, and whether a new setting still needs a restart. - The listen address, API key and admin credentials are managed by the plugin; changing them in the admin page has no effect. - **Gemini Web:** The backend ignores system proxies and `HTTP_PROXY`. Enter your proxy URL when prompted at the start of "One-click local setup", set the `proxy` plugin option or `GEMINI_WEB_PROXY` environment variable, or add it to the proxy pool in the local admin panel at `http://127.0.0.1:8083/admin` (password is `adminToken` in `secrets.json` inside the data directory). - *Note:* When using a proxy pool, send one request with a newly added account so the backend binds it to a proxy, then re-add it via "Add an existing Google account from the local backend" to load its email and usage (SOCKS proxies are not supported for usage reads). **Connecting a self-hosted backend:** If you already run `gemini-web2api-go` or `AIStudio2API` yourself, select **Connect an existing backend / AIStudio2API** during sign-in and provide its `/v1` URL and API key. **Refreshing the model list:** After upgrading the plugin, run `magpie provider models gemini-web` to refresh available models.
🛠️ AI Studio CLI Commands (service status, re-login, offline install)
**When the local service starts and stops:** - It starts in the background when the plugin loads (when Magpie opens, for example); after that, a request or a usage card refresh starts it again if it isn't running. - It is a process of its own: **quitting Magpie doesn't stop it**, and Magpie picks it up again the next time it opens. - To stop it, use `studio:stop` below (or the full command the card or an error gives). A stop lasts until the next request, which starts it again. When a plugin error asks you to run a command, it includes the full ready-to-copy path. From the plugin directory, you can also run: | Command | Description | | :--- | :--- | | `npm run studio:status` | Show local service and account status | | `npm run studio:start` / `studio:stop` | Start / stop the local service | | `npm run studio:clean` | Stop the service and remove downloaded binaries & Camoufox (keeps accounts & config) | | `npm run studio:login` | Add a Google account | | `npm run studio:relogin -- []` | Re-authenticate an expired account (argument optional if only one) | | `npm run studio:install -- --archive ` | Offline install from a pre-downloaded archive | | `node scripts/studio.mjs import ` | Import existing accounts while the service is stopped | | `npm run studio:smoke` | Run a live acceptance check (consumes account quota) |
🔒 Security, Data Directories & Backend Version Management (logs, rollback, macOS Native Task)
**Security & data directories:** - Both backends listen on `127.0.0.1` only. Cookies and sessions remain on your machine; Magpie stores only a locally generated API key. - **Gemini Web data directory:** `~/.local/share/magpie-gemini-web` (override with `GEMINI_WEB_DATA_DIR`), logs at `backend.log`. Supports macOS, Linux, and Windows (x64 / arm64). - **AI Studio data directory:** `~/.local/share/magpie-ai-studio` (override with `AI_STUDIO_DATA_DIR`), logs at `backend.log` (rotated on next start after exceeding 10 MB). Uses port 2048 by default (or picks a free port and saves it in `config.json`). Supports macOS, Linux (x64 / arm64), and Windows x64. - **Uninstalling & cleaning downloaded assets:** Removing the plugin in Magpie (or running `npm run studio:clean` / `npm run backend:clean`) stops the local services and deletes the downloaded `AIStudio2API`, `Camoufox`, and `gemini-web2api-go` binaries and archives. - `auth/`, `gemini.db`, `config.json`, `.env`, and `secrets.json` are kept so reinstalling the plugin or sending a new request restores the backend on demand without signing in or importing cookies again; to prevent automatic reinstallation permanently, remove the sign-in in Magpie or delete `config.json` / `secrets.json`. - Default data directories are shared per OS user; set separate `AI_STUDIO_DATA_DIR` and `GEMINI_WEB_DATA_DIR` when running multiple isolated Magpie config directories so removing the plugin in one does not clean another's shared binaries. - Gemini Web takes at most 2 requests at once per sign-in (AI Studio 1), adjustable in Magpie's provider settings. Google account rate-limiting or flagging cannot be completely ruled out—use at your own risk. **AI Studio upgrades and model selection:** - The plugin pins SHA-256-verified `v0.3.5-magpie.1`, based on upstream `v0.3.5`. Upgrade the plugin to update the backend. Official releases at or below that upstream version, and managed backends an older plugin installed, are upgraded on the next managed startup, preserving accounts, port and sign-in credentials. - Account priority ordering (`ACCOUNT_ORDER`) and per-model account bindings (`MODEL_ACCOUNTS`) from 0.3.3, as well as API key account bindings and hedge model selections from 0.2.19, are preserved. Settings saved in the admin page, including upstream defaults, survive plugin restarts. Hedge requests remain off by default; enable them and select models in the admin page if needed. - For users upgrading from 0.2.18 with `auto` enabled, hedging now applies only to `FIRST_EVENT_HEDGE_MODELS`, defaulting to Argon when that list is absent. Saving in the admin page fixes the current defaults in the file; later upstream default changes require manual adjustment. When taking over an official 0.2.19 sparse configuration, missing settings follow the plugin's initialization rules (for example, hedging becomes `off`). See the [upgrade compatibility notes](docs/studio-release.md#0219-升级兼容). - **Online updates are disabled in the managed backend on macOS, Linux, and Windows.** The admin page says updates are managed by magpie-gemini-web; the update endpoint returns HTTP 409 and update checks do not contact GitHub. Independently managed external servers are unaffected. See [docs/studio-release.md](docs/studio-release.md) for how the managed build is made and reproduced. - Managed Unix installs still attempt to set `package/` to `0555` as additional file protection. Permission failures do not block service, and disabling online updates does not depend on permissions. To reset by manually deleting the data directory, stop the service first, then run `chmod -R u+w "/package"` before deleting it; replace `` with the actual path. - If a newer or custom version is installed, the plugin reports a conflict with `stop`, `install`, and `start` commands carrying the correct `--data-dir`. Stop can recover a changed listener PID and verifies its executable path before signaling it. If HTTP is down but the process is still alive, the plugin refuses to reinstall or launch a second process. - When stopped, a replaced executable is restored from the verified pinned archive; failed verification never launches the replacement. Existing account and runtime data files are kept, but **an older backend may not read data migrated by a newer version**. Before manually downgrading, stop the service and back up the entire data directory, including `auth/` and `runtime/requests.db`. If data migration is known to have occurred, update the plugin to match the newer backend. - The backend's base request deadline and the plugin's default response/stream-idle timeout are 30 minutes (override via `studio.requestTimeoutMs`). This allows long non-streaming replies to finish collecting on the server. A stalled backend can also take 30 minutes to time out, and its single worker can hold up later requests. Cancel a request or choose a shorter timeout when needed; shorter limits can interrupt valid long replies. Upstream controls deadline scaling for automatic continuation. - Source review of the locally installed Magpie `v0.1.1285` (`d783df46`) found no shorter fixed total timeout on this plugin's generation path: `Provider.Do → plugin.Fetch → loader.fetch` bypasses the ordinary HTTP transport's 10-minute response-header timeout. The gateway's 5-minute `IdleTimeout` applies between requests. Clients or reverse proxies can impose shorter limits; this was not a 30-minute end-to-end waiting test. - Deep Research models (`deep-research-preview-04-2026`, `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026`) are supported: listed when signed in with a Google AI Pro / Ultra account; the backend adapts asynchronous Interactions tasks onto `/v1/chat/completions` streaming (including reasoning and built-in server-side search), without client `tool_call` (Function Calling) or `temperature`. - Models with `-build` or `assistant_route` are filtered out: they inject the Build coding assistant's own system prompt and are not offered as ordinary Agent models. Chat requests are timed by silence: while Google queues a request it sends a heartbeat every 60 s, and the backend waits through it for the first words. 快速开始 在 Magpie 插件市场安装 **magpie-gemini-web** 后，按需登录以下任一（或两个）Provider。插件会自动下载对应后端、校验 SHA-256 并在后台自启，无需安装 Go 或其它依赖。 ### 方式一：Google AI Studio (`ai-studio`) 1. 在 Magpie 中登录 **Google AI Studio**，选择 **「用 Google 账号登录（推荐）」**。 2. 插件准备本地服务后，会在同一页面自动进入 **账号导入／登录**。选择 **Chrome 导入、粘贴 Cookie 或浏览器登录**；无需另装服务或复制 API key，多账号只需在导入界面勾选一次。 3. 本次任务全部成功后，插件会**自动完成 Magpie 配置**，无需返回连接页再选账号。导入一个账号时保存该账号，批量导入时保存本次账号组，部分失败后仅重试失败账号也会保留此前成功的账号；继续使用原有的 `ai-studio` Provider、模型、图片生成和额度卡片。 4. **后续管理**：再次点击「用 Google 账号登录」，可添加新账号、为本机已有账号单独建卡，或重新登录过期账号。也可选择 **「直接打开 Google 登录窗口」**，沿用独立浏览器登录流程。 首次使用需下载本地服务（约 40 MB）；浏览器登录和专用重登入口需要 Camoufox（约 300 MB）。也可通过「添加 Google 账号」的 Chrome / Cookie / 调试浏览器导入更新同一账号的登录状态，保留文件绑定与续签材料。Magpie 最多等 10 分钟，下载时间也算在内。自动流程超时或取消时会停止本次尚未完成的任务，保留已导入的账号；其他窗口的任务不受影响。连不上 GitHub 时先设置 `studio.proxy`。 内置后端 `0.3.5-magpie.1` 已包含自动登录补丁。尚在运行的旧后端会兼容原来的手动连接流程；停止旧进程后，下次托管启动会更新后端。 ### 方式二：Gemini Web (`gemini-web`) 1. 在 Magpie 中登录 **Gemini Web**，选择 **「一键配置本地 Gemini Web（推荐）」**（若访问 Google 需要代理，可在第一步提示中直接填写代理地址，例如 `http://127.0.0.1:7890`，无需代理或已配置代理池可留空）。 2. 按提示填写 **Google 账号索引**：复制 Cookie 的同一窗口地址若为 `/u/4/app`，填 `4`；单账号会话可留空（`0`）。无痕窗口中的索引可能不同，不能直接沿用日常窗口的编号。然后在浏览器**无痕 / 隐私窗口**（推荐 Firefox）获取 Cookie： 1. 访问 并登录 Google 账号； 2. 按 `F12`（macOS 按 `⌥⌘I`）切到 **Network（网络）**，刷新页面； 3. 点击任意 `gemini.google.com` 请求 → **Headers** → **Request Headers**，复制 `cookie` 的值粘贴回 Magpie； 4. **直接关闭无痕窗口，不要点退出登录**（点退出会使 Cookie 失效）。 3. 插件验证账号可用后即完成登录。想添加更多账号，重复上述步骤即可。 > **升级后提示后端不支持登录时绑定代理？** 旧后台进程可能仍在运行。请按提示先退出 Magpie，停止对应的 `gemini-web2api-go` 进程（Windows：任务管理器 → 详细信息 → `gemini-web2api-go.exe`），再运行提示中的完整安装命令。它会保留账号和配置，并切换到插件的托管后端；如下载需要代理，先设置 `GEMINI_WEB_PROXY`。完成后重新打开 Magpie 登录。 > **为什么必须用无痕窗口？** 后端会定时刷新会话来保活。若与日常浏览器共用同一登录会话，Google 会将整个会话作废，导致你的浏览器退出所有 Google 服务。使用无痕窗口（或单独准备 Google 小号）可提供独立会话。 --- ## 多账号与额度卡片 - **账号额度卡片**：单个 Google 账号以邮箱命名；AI Studio 批量导入以账号组建卡，不同组独立统计，重复导入同组不会因账号顺序变化而新增卡片。 - *旧版迁移（Gemini Web）*：若后端里已有早期版本添加的账号，在登录时选 **「添加本地后端里已有的 Google 账号」** 即可生成独立卡片，随后可删掉旧的 `API key …` 汇总卡片。 - **账号池自动调度**：请求实际使用哪个账号由本地后端决定（Gemini Web 在账号池中轮流挑选；AI Studio 先用一个，进入冷却再切下一个，可在管理页或通过 `studio.accountOrder`、`studio.modelAccounts` 指定账号优先顺序与模型专属账号池）。在 Magpie 界面切换卡片不会改变后端的账号调度。 - **用量刷新说明**： - `gemini-web`：仅一键配置的本地后端可读取用量。Magpie 每次来查都会向 Google 重新读取（同一账号 30 秒内只读一次），点刷新即显示最新额度，包括在 Gemini 官方 App、网页或其他设备上的用量。Magpie 自己来查的频率：用量页或菜单栏的额度面板开着时约每分钟一次；菜单栏显示任何一家额度时随菜单栏更新（默认每 3 分钟）；经 Magpie 转发请求时最多每分钟一次；都没有时不查。读取失败后 10 分钟内不自动重试，这期间点刷新会立即重试，若未生效再点一次。 - `ai-studio`：AI Studio 不提供剩余总额度，卡片会展示当前账号正在冷却的模型、恢复时间或重新登录提示。 --- ## 图片生成（AI Studio） `ai-studio` 会列出账号可用的 Nano Banana 系列图像模型（如 `gemini-3.1-flash-image`、`gemini-3-pro-image`），供 Magpie 的图片生成使用。**需要 Magpie v0.1.2075 及以上**：从这个版本起，Magpie 才会把插件的 Gemini 图像模型列为出图模型。 **让 Agent 出图**（pi、Claude Code、Codex 等都一样）： 1. **选画图模型**：Magpie 设置的 **Images → Image generation** 会直接列出这些模型，选中一个（如 `ai-studio/gemini-nano-banana-2.1`），或保持 Automatic（自动）。不用在模型列表里勾选它们。 2. **把画图工具交给 Agent**：点这一行下面的 **Give agents Magpie Image…**，在打开的 Library 里勾选要出图的 Agent，然后新开一个 Agent 会话。Library 被关掉时，这里显示的是 **Turn on the Library**，先点它。也可以用命令行：`magpie library mcp add magpie-image magpie mcp image agents=pi`（多个 Agent 用逗号隔开，如 `agents=pi,claude`）。 3. **照常对话**：Agent 继续用平常的对话模型，跟它说「画一张……」就行。它会调用 `generate_image` 工具，用第 1 步选的模型出图，图片存进项目的 `generated-images/` 文件夹；带参考图就是改图。 - **别把图像模型选成对话模型**：Magpie 目前会把能出图的插件模型也留在对话模型列表里（[yetone/magpie#2792](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2792)）。选了也看不到图：pi 等 Agent 的回复里放不下图片，模型画出的图会被直接丢掉，模型却以为已经发出去了。它们也不支持工具调用，上下文只有 32K–128K。 - **在命令行出图**：`magpie tool generate_image "a magpie on a branch, watercolour" --size 16:9 -o magpie.png`，加 `--model ai-studio/gemini-3-pro-image` 可以临时换模型。终端里找不到 `magpie` 命令时（第 2 步的命令也一样），在 Magpie 设置的 **Command line** 一行点 **Add to PATH**，再开一个新终端。 - **尺寸**：`size` 决定宽高比：写比例（如 `16:9`、`1:4`）时，模型支持就照用，不支持就取它支持的最接近的比例；写 `1536x1024` 这样的尺寸时，Magpie 先换成最接近的常用比例。`quality` 对这些模型不起作用。 - 不需要图像模型时，可以用 `studio.imageModels` 关掉（见下方选项）。 --- ## # Gemini Native Task 桥接与 Magpie 扩展

本目录包含针对 macOS 原生 Gemini App 任务模式（Task Mode / Argon）的本地常驻守护进程与 Magpie 扩展插件。此实现为 Alpha 预览版本，提供文本对话及串行 OpenAI Function Calling 工具调用能力。

## 前置要求与环境限制

1. **操作系统**：仅支持 macOS（arm64），需已安装 `/Applications/Gemini.app`（版本 `1.128.14.1166`，SHA-256 `8cd89234b23182234e8e211e1449ae44e0a831b2185e98f4d1371a83c66f8964`）。
2. **已登录账户**：需在 Gemini.app 中已登录可用账户，桥接器通过只读 Keychain API 读取原生凭据并执行 OAuth 续期。
3. **App 必须退出**：在运行原生 Task 任务时，本机运行的 Gemini.app 进程必须处于退出状态（`pgrep -x Gemini` 必须为空），避免长连接与设备状态冲突。
4. **抓取模板**：首次配置需要有效的会话头与消息模板（`task-headers.json`、`tool-headers.json`、`task-template.bin`、`turn-template.bin`）。`x-server-token` 与设备凭据暂未实现自动续期，需由已抓取模板手工提供。

## 架构与行为特性

- **模型标识**：网关模型 ID 为 `gemini-web/gemini-task-argon`（本地服务模型 ID 为 `gemini-task-argon`）。
- **工具调用**：支持 OpenAI Function Calling 格式的串行工具调用（单轮至多 1 个工具调用），由客户端执行并回传结果。工具声明映射至 `agent_bridge` 服务。单个 Task 上限 32 次工具调用（非整个会话全局上限）。
- **并发与超时**：全局同一时刻仅允许 1 个活跃 Task。任务全局超时为 240 秒，单次工具等待超时为 50 秒。无断线自动重连或重放机制。
- **会话与持久化**：调用 Magpie 网关时必须提供稳定的 `X-Session-ID`，由插件的 `chat.headers` 将它转换为本机服务使用的 `X-Gemini-Session`。直接访问本机服务时使用 `X-Gemini-Session`。仅在网关传 `X-Magpie-Session` 不足以保证重试和续轮使用同一 ID。会话状态持久化于私有目录（`~/.local/share/gemini-native-task/sessions/*.json`，权限 `0600`）。
- **容量与历史限制**：单个会话最多缓存 256 次请求记录，本地最多存储 128 个会话。不支持透明的历史压缩、修改或分支分叉（修改历史需开启新会话）。
- **中断恢复与取消**：守护进程重启时，未完成的会话将标记为 `interrupted`，不会继续重放或悬挂。本地取消仅中止本地工作线程与流，服务端不保证原生任务取消。
- **协议与参数说明**：
  - 允许传入 `system` / `developer` 角色消息，通过精确的前置提示词进行转译兼容，但服务端无原生系统角色通道。
  - `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` 仅作为兼容性提示词建议注入，服务端无硬性切断。
  - 不提供 Token 用量统计（Token Usage）。
  - 流式响应（SSE）按阶段（工具调用 / 最终答案）缓冲输出，非逐字 Token 流。
  - 不支持采样参数（temperature / top_p）或结构化输出（JSON Schema response format）。
  - 原生对话记录保留在 Google 服务端。

2026-10-15：已执行通过 41 项 Python 测试和 12 项 Node 测试；真实 Magpie `0.1.1244` 的隔离环境完成了插件安装、本地连接、模型发现及 8 个 HTTP 请求的工具往返测试。该网关测试使用模拟原生上游，包含两次串行工具、最终答案重试、错误会话/调用 ID 拒绝、旧工具阶段拒绝和下一轮用户消息。

2026-10-15：通过 `magpie-gemini-web` 0.4.0 的 Task 登录方式（直接加载插件，未经 Magpie 网关）完成了一次真实 Argon 工具往返：模型返回 `Read` 工具调用（19.2 秒），回传工具结果后得到正确的最终答案（13.7 秒）。此前真实 Task 请求曾被 Google 以 `Remy quota exhausted`（gRPC 8）拒绝，服务将该错误映射为 `native_quota_exhausted`，不会自动重发 Task。

# Backend releases

The plugin's default backend is built from the upstream commit and toolchain recorded in `lib/backend-release.json`, with `patches/argon.patch` applied. The builder overrides the backend's displayed version with the release version. Six binaries are pinned by SHA-256 in the same JSON file. The build does not include the developer's uncommitted backend sources, local data or credentials.

For a new backend release:

1. Choose a new backend version and tag in `lib/backend-release.json`. Never replace files under an already published backend tag: older plugins pin those hashes. Update the upstream commit or patch when needed.
2. Run `node scripts/backend-release.mjs --write-pins`. It extracts a clean upstream tree, applies the patch, runs Go tests, cross-compiles all six targets and writes the resulting pins. It uses a local `backend-source` Git object database if available; otherwise it fetches the pinned public commit in a temporary directory.
3. Run `npm test` and `node scripts/backend-smoke.mjs`. The smoke test uses a temporary data directory, checks the actual executable's version and hash, starts it on a spare loopback port, checks authentication and model discovery, and verifies reuse. It uses no Google account and takes the tokenizer's offline fallback.
4. Commit the release metadata, installer changes, tests and documentation. Run the **Verify backend release** GitHub Actions workflow at that commit. It rebuilds on native macOS, Linux and Windows runners for both architectures, compares the pinned hashes, and runs the installation/startup smoke test. Wait for all jobs to pass.
5. Create a private draft under the pinned backend tag. Attach all six binaries, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `build.json`, the patched source archive and `LICENSE-UPSTREAM` from `backend-build/release`. If local binary uploads are unreliable, run **Upload verified backend release** with the successful verification run ID: it downloads the six CI artifacts, checks every committed hash, and uploads missing executables to the draft. Existing assets must match exactly; published releases cannot be modified by this workflow. Include the upstream commit and patch SHA-256 in the release notes, then publish the complete draft. Keep backend-only releases from replacing the plugin release as GitHub's latest release.
6. Verify public asset downloads against the committed pins. Run `node scripts/backend-smoke.mjs --download` to test the actual default download URL on the host platform.
7. Bump and publish the plugin package only after the backend assets are publicly available. Inspect `npm pack --dry-run`; the npm package contains release metadata and patch/build scripts, but no executables, local databases or credentials. Attach the exact published npm tarball to the plugin's GitHub release as well.

Reproduce a release without changing its pins:

```bash
npm run backend:release:build
```

Build just the host target and compare its hash:

```bash
node scripts/backend-release.mjs --target=host --verify
```

The metadata records `CGO_ENABLED=0`, the exact Go toolchain, upstream commit, patch hash and build flags. The binary hashes are reproducible; the source archive is supplied for inspection and is not promised to have a reproducible gzip timestamp. The source archive includes upstream's license, and `LICENSE-UPSTREAM` is also supplied as a separate asset.

Existing running processes are left alone to avoid interrupting requests. Once an old official backend is stopped, automatic startup installs the optimized build while preserving configuration, secrets and the database. A download or checksum failure keeps the old file and never starts an unverified replacement.

New cookie imports require the running backend to advertise `capabilities.account_proxy_binding: true` at `/`. The plugin checks this before changing the proxy pool and again before submitting a cookie, so a reused older or upstream backend cannot silently ignore `proxy_id`. Unsupported builds receive instructions to stop the old process and run the installed plugin's CLI with `install --data-dir=<path>`. This explicitly selects the optimized channel, including for previous upstream or custom-build installations. The check does not interrupt existing conversations. Release smoke verifies the capability and actual proxy selection; version strings alone do not establish support.

An explicit `npm run backend:install:upstream` installs the pinned upstream v4.28.0 and persists `upstream` in `backend-channel.json`. Automatic startup respects that choice. `npm run backend:install` returns to the optimized channel. Stop a running backend before replacing it, particularly on Windows. Explicit local Argon builds remain trusted through their existing build manifest.

插件使用 `0.3.5-magpie.1`，基于 AIStudio2API `v0.3.5`（`bab7209eef0d5a8f9baed4652d7e4158a3adad7b`）。上游版本、commit、Go 版本、C/C++ 工具链、SpiderMonkey 与 libwebp 静态库（`toolchains`）、补丁列表、安装包及二进制 SHA-256 均记录在 `lib/studio-release.json`。`upstream.camoufox` 是这个 commit 要求的 Camoufox 版本（上游 `internal/camoufoxnative/download.go` 里的 `camoufoxRelease`），更新上游 commit 时要一起核对，构建脚本发现不一致会报错。MIT 许可见 `LICENSE-AISTUDIO`。

## 插件账号管理接入

推荐登录入口由 `lib/studio-connect.mjs` 显示安装进度，随后在同一标签页自动进入随包上游的账号导入／登录界面。上游登录模式展示 Chrome 导入、Cookie 导入、调试浏览器会话导入和浏览器登录，隐藏远程配对。专用重登入口显示加载、错误或账号缺失状态，使用隔离浏览器重新登录。v0.3.5 也支持通过添加账号入口导入同一账号来更新认证状态；`studio-0.3.5-signin-reauth.patch` 修正此前不支持覆盖导入的提示。单个账号成功后直接保存原有 `managed: true` 的 `ai-studio` 登录；批量导入成功后保存 `metadata.accounts` 和带账号集合摘要的 `metadata.email`，使不同分组不会互相覆盖；同组以不同顺序重试保持相同标识。额度卡片的账号和冷却记录都按本次账号组过滤。此元数据不改变后端的全局选号、API key 绑定或模型绑定规则。模型、图片和用量继续走原插件，不调用 `magpie://import` 创建其他供应商。

`patches/studio-0.3.4-magpie-signin.patch` 给管理页增加由 URL fragment 开启的登录模式，并给账号任务增加 `client_id`、成功条目的规范 `account_id` 和 `GET /api/accounts/tasks` 的 `magpie_signin: 1` 能力标识。每次登录使用独立随机标识；只有当前页面提交的完整成功任务能完成认证。插件从后台任务取得账号 ID，再重新读取账号列表校验。已有账号、其他窗口任务、失败或部分失败任务均不会自动完成当前登录。部分失败可只重试失败账号：插件按本次标识累积每个已成功条目的账号 ID，最终成功时合并、去重并重新校验。登录模式暂不提供关闭失败任务的按钮，避免插件观察前删除成功条目；已观察到的成功条目即使之后从任务列表移除也会保留。刷新页面保留登录标识；关闭浏览器后，插件仍能跟踪已启动任务。

管理会话通过本机 HTTP 响应的 `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api` Cookie 交给浏览器。两个服务均限定为 `http://127.0.0.1`；Cookie 按主机共享，不按端口隔离。临时页使用随机路径、严格 Host / 写操作 Origin 检查和 CSP，状态接口不返回 API key、管理密码或 Google Cookie。上游 fragment 仅含关联标识、本机回程地址、截止时间及可选目标账号；不放凭据。自动流程取消或超时只取消本次标识下仍运行的任务，保留已导入账号。结束后不再发放管理会话，两分钟后关闭临时服务，并清理本次标识下的成功、失败及未结束任务记录。回程页的状态请求会等待正在进行的检查或立即检查任务，无需额外等待轮询周期。

**发行状态：** `0.3.5-magpie.1` 包含自动登录补丁，正式 pin 由五平台 CI 生成并在全新 runner 上严格复现。插件探测到不支持任务关联的旧后端时，使用 `lib/studio-connect-legacy.mjs` 保持手动连接流程。用户无需额外安装、填 URL 或复制密钥。

候选构建配置位于 `scripts/studio-signin-candidate.json`，空的 `binaries` 条目表示尚无发行哈希，不是可安装的发行清单。普通本机构建可验证补丁和 UI（不会改动当前 pin）：

```sh
node scripts/studio-release.mjs --manifest=scripts/studio-signin-candidate.json --target=host
```

正式五平台构建使用 `studio.yml` 的 `write_pins=true` 和 `signin_candidate=true`，从固定工具链生成 candidate artifacts。收集阶段会验证所有构建记录的上游、补丁哈希和工具链，再产生完整 `candidate-pins`。将该文件替换 `lib/studio-release.json`，执行常规五平台验证并发布后端，最后发布插件。也可用 `scripts/studio-pins.mjs --manifest=<candidate.json> <build-record.json>...` 合并本地候选记录；缺平台或输入不一致会拒绝。不要把本机 beta Xcode 的验证构建哈希写入正式 pin。

测试覆盖当前任务隔离、批量导入、部分失败重试、完成时重新校验、重新登录身份限制、来源检查、旧后端回退、取消和超时；上游补丁另含任务关联、前端回程地址、窄视口导航、路由锁定及重登状态渲染测试。Windows CI 运行全部 `studio*.test.mjs`，候选配置随 npm 包提供。构建脚本同时运行这些测试、上游 Go 测试、前端 lint 和类型检查。真实 Google 登录和 Windows Chrome 导入仍需带账号验证。
